findings.passage: “There’s a fear that people have that you’re going to disenfranchise somebody. And it’s a healthy fear,” he said. “You don’t want to disenfranchise people … but at some point you carry those concerns to the point where you wind up paralyzed with no action.”
findings.note: Quoted by the Mississippi Free Press in an interview about his bill HB 586, which would have checked registered voters for non-citizens. He speaks of the worry that such checks could disenfranchise voters and says concern should not stop action.

findings.passage: “What the bill effectively did was change how the state verified new registered voters. It would check everybody on the back side,” Eubanks said.
findings.note: Quoted by the Mississippi Free Press. He describes HB 586 as moving the citizenship check to after registration, covering everybody.

findings.passage: “If you have no faith in your system, how can you have faith in your leaders?” he said.
findings.note: Quoted by the Mississippi Free Press. The article says he argues that measures like HB 586 restore faith in the electoral process; this is his own line on that point.

Per the Mississippi Free Press (not the legislature's page), he introduced House Bill 586, which would have directed the Statewide Elections Management System to check identification databases for registered non-citizens. The bill died.
